purpose: Targeted follow-up of three USAAF 1988 source-line cases where unit arrival or liaison activity predates declared airfield operational date. Distinguish dated official unit station from a field code, a temporary landing area, and an operational strip.
evidenceRules: 1988 USAF Johnson Part I and II reflect one study; two pages are not two independent sources.
Official USAF Maurer 1982 squadron histories are retrospective lineage compilations, not contemporary squadron operation-record books.
Do not assign an individual aircraft, airfield code, runway coordinate or group-wide strength from a reconnaissance/advance detachment.
Separate district-level unit stationing from exact physical airfield occupancy and from the airfield operational declaration.
Where a historical airfield began in March 1945, do not render its 1944 regional unit records as pins on the later runway.
Do not infer actual operational aircraft strength, sorties, kills or losses from presence-only records.

cases.researchConclusion: The August report refers to a scouting/reconnaissance detachment, not evidence that the 365th Fighter Group was operationally based at A-44. Construction began only in the second half of August; 367th FG began operating there in September. Exact August physical position, arrival day and aircraft use remain unconfirmed.

cases.researchConclusion: A USAF official squadron history confirms the 125th Liaison Squadron was stationed in the Maastricht area from 21 Oct 1944, followed by Mönchengladbach from 9 Mar 1945. NIMH says airfield Y-44 near Beek was newly constructed in early 1945 and operational from 28 Mar 1945. The Johnson unit date is a regional/lineage association, NOT proof of operation from the not-yet-built Beek runway in 1944. Local accounts report separate facilities at Geusseltpark and Sint-Pietersberg and possible March 1945 liaison aircraft on the new field; latter needs dated unit-specific corroboration.

cases.researchConclusion: The 112th Liaison Squadron official USAF history dates a FLIGHT at Namur from 26 Oct 1944 to approximately 11 Feb 1945, while its parent squadron remained stationed at Buc, France. Belgian veteran aviation history states construction at Temploux–Suarlée started September 1944 and the undeclared landing strip was already used in October, before the formal 22 Feb 1945 airfield declaration. These dates describe distinct operations; no reason to change either date. The precise pre-hardened landing point relative to the eventual runway remains unverified.
